newsitem.title: CHINA: China to draw foreign firms to hinterland.
newsitem.headline: China to draw foreign firms to hinterland.

text.p: China is considering drafting preferential measures to attract foreign investors to the nation's central and western regions, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

"China will consider drafting preferential industrial policies in the hinterland to stimulate foreign investment," Xinhua quoted Vice Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Liu Xiangdong as saying.

Beijing would encourage overseas investment in natural resources, agriculture and animal husbandry in the central and western areas, Liu was quoted as telling a Chinese trade society on Tuesday. China would make it easier for domestic companies seeking cooperation with foreign investors to get loans for projects in the region while overseas firms would be allowed to sell most of their products on domestic markets, he said.
Economic development of the hinterland was essential to ensuring China's solid growth into the next century, he said.

"To ignore economic growth and the use of foreign capital in the region will affect the national economy by the end of this century," he said. China's central and western regions are rich in natural resources but economic growth and foreign investment lag far behind the booming eastern coastal regions.
